extracted.intended_audience: students of analysis / ordinary differential equations (advanced undergraduate/graduate), mechanics students
extracted.subtask_description: Methods and rules for solving linear ordinary differential equations with constant coefficients (homogeneous and nonhomogeneous), and for reducing and integrating systems of ODEs; includes undetermined coefficients, treatment of multiple and complex roots, first integrals, and series methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chaque racine donne autant de solutions que sa multiplicité
rubrics_metrics.description: "En résumé, chaque racine de φ(r) donne un nombre de solutions distinctes, égal à son degré de multiplicité : on aura donc, dans tous les cas, n solutions distinctes ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If r is a root of multiplicity p of the characteristic polynomial φ(r), the differential equation has p independent solutions; the general integral is formed by combining all such solutions to obtain n arbitrary constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forme des solutions pour racine d'ordre p
rubrics_metrics.description: "Si r est racine d'ordre p de φ(r), l'équation différentielle admet les p solutions e^{r x}, x e^{r x}, ..., x^{p-1} e^{r x}."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated by substituting v(x)e^{r x} and using identities obtained by differentiating; apply the identities (12) iteratively. Example: double root gives e^{r x} et x e^{r x}; triple root gives e^{r x}, x e^{r x}, x^2 e^{r x}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traitement des racines complexes — récupération de solutions réelles
rubrics_metrics.description: When characteristic roots are complex (e.g. r = α ± iβ) the corresponding real independent solutions can be taken as cos(β x) e^{α x} and sin(β x) e^{α x}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: replace e^{(α+iβ)x} and e^{(α-iβ)x} by their real and imaginary parts: e^{α x} cos(β x), e^{α x} sin(β x). To eliminate imaginaries, replace complex constants by conjugate imaginary constants so the general real solution is expressed with real arbitrary constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Réduction par connaissance d'une intégrale particulière (y=Y+H)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Si l'on connaît une intégrale particulière H de cette équation, on peut ramener son intégration à l'intégration de la même équation sans second membre." (y = Y + H)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute y = Y + H; since φ(H)=X (the RHS), substitution yields φ(Y)=0, so Y satisfies the homogeneous equation. The general solution is then Y (general solution of homogeneous) plus the known particular H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Méthode des coefficients indéterminés pour deuxième membre polynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: "Si ... le deuxième membre est un polynôme P(x) de degré p, il existe une solution particulière u de cette équation, qui est un polynôme en x de degré égal ou supérieur à p."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try a polynomial u of degree p with undetermined coefficients; substitute into the left-hand operator and equate coefficients to determine them. If the characteristic polynomial makes the trial fail (e.g. zero root), increase the degree (try p+1, p+2, ... as needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cas exponentiel Ae^{a x} — choix du forme particulière et exception
rubrics_metrics.description: For RHS Ae^{a x} try a particular solution of form C e^{a x} (constant C determined by substituting). Exception: if a is a root of φ(r), then use multiplied forms: if a is a root of multiplicity p, try x^{p} times e^{a x}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute φ(a); if φ(a)≠0 then C = A/φ(a). If a is a simple root take x e^{a x}; if double root take x^{2} e^{a x}, etc. Identities (21) justify these choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traitement du cas général P(x) + somme d'exponentielles (superposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Pour trouver une solution particulière u de cette équation, on détermine d'abord des fonctions u_1,u_2,... vérifiant les relations φ(u_1)=P(x), φ(u_2)=Ae^{a x}, ... puis u = u_1+u_2+..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linearity: find particular solutions for each independent term of the second member (polynomial and each exponential/term), taking into account multiplicities; sum them to obtain a particular solution for the whole RHS. Then reduce to homogeneous equation for remainder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilisation de la représentation exponentielle pour fonctions trigonométriques
rubrics_metrics.description: Trigonometric RHS (cos x, sin x) are handled by writing them as combinations of exponentials and applying the exponential-case method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: cos x = (e^{ix}+e^{-ix})/2; treat each exponential term with its own a, check whether ±i are roots of φ(r), and if necessary multiply by x^p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Méthode des essais et identification des coefficients (détail pratique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitute a trial function (polynomial of chosen degree or linear combination of exponentials times powers of x) into the differential operator; the result is a polynomial/expression whose coefficients must match the RHS, giving algebraic equations for undetermined coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show choosing minimal necessary degree (or increasing if operator annihilates trial). Solve linear system for coefficients; some leading coefficients may be arbitrary if kernel allows, then pick convenient values and proceed to determine Y and the general integral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Réduction d'un système de n équations du 1er ordre à une ODE d'ordre n
rubrics_metrics.description: "On montre que l'intégration du système se ramène à l'intégration d'une équation différentielle d'ordre n, suivie d'opérations algébriques."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate the first equation successively, replace derivatives of other variables by their expressions from the system, obtain n relations, eliminate the n−1 other unknowns to get a single nth-order ODE in y_1. Integrate that ODE, then retrieve other functions algebraically without further integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cas particulier : deux équations du premier ordre → équation du deuxième ordre
rubrics_metrics.description: For two first-order equations in two unknowns, derive the first equation, eliminate the other unknown to obtain a second-order ODE for one function; then recover the other by algebraic substitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit recipe given in N°396: differentiate, eliminate z and z', obtain second-order ODE; integrate to get Y (general integral), then substitute back to find the other function(s) with the same arbitrary constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intégration par séries (Maclaurin / Taylor) et détermination par conditions initiales
rubrics_metrics.description: "Les coefficients de ces séries sont des fonctions des n constantes arbitraires ... il suffit de donner les valeurs qu'elles doivent prendre pour une valeur déterminée x_0 de la variable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute successive derivatives from the system to express Taylor coefficients in terms of the initial values (the n arbitrary constants). If the series converge, they define the solution. One may take Maclaurin or Taylor about any x_0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intégrales premières — définition et usage pour abaisser le nombre d'inconnues
rubrics_metrics.description: "On appelle intégrale première d'un système ... une équation entre la variable indépendante, les fonctions inconnues ... et une constante arbitraire, qui se trouve satisfaite en vertu des équations (5) ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A first integral is a relation f(x,y_1,...,y_n)=C whose derivative vanishes by virtue of the system. Knowing one first integral allows expressing one variable in terms of others and C and reduces the number of unknown functions by one; knowing k independent first integrals reduces by k. Distinctness is defined (one integral not a function of others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Réduction d'équations d'ordre quelconque à système du premier ordre (introduire dérivées comme inconnues)
rubrics_metrics.description: To integrate systems of higher-order equations, convert them to a first-order system by introducing successive derivatives as new unknown functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example in mechanics: second-order equations for x,y,z are turned into six first-order equations by setting velocities as new unknowns. The general integral of the first-order system is determined by giving initial values of all introduced unknowns (positions and velocities). Each known first integral reduces the number of unknowns by one.
